mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations rise sharply as measured by CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the GDP and housing weakness coincides with a simultaneous surge in labor market strength (PAYEMS).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress earnings expectations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.5% for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL does not fall in the same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when industrial production (INDPRO) is simultaneously rising by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong demand growth as measured by RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 300k new jobs per month for two consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tightening labor market that boosts wage pressure and ultimately reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 300000 for two consecutive months AND UNRATE unchanged
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation (CPIAUCSL) is simultaneously falling sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the 5-year average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-year average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of more than 0.75 percentage points, in the absence of a concurrent surge in inflation (CPIAUCSL), signals an aggressive policy shift that immediately raises risk-free rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps > 0.75% in one month AND CPIAUCSL does not rise in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the spike is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in inflation expectations.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.7% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based manufacturing recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the industrial rebound is accompanied by a simultaneous sharp rise in input costs (not directly observable in available proxies).
